chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan ibn Yahya from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Muhrim (person in Ihram) who has intercourse with his wife, he said: If he has fully penetrated her, then upon him is a camel and Hajj next year; and if he has not fully penetrated her, then upon him is a camel and he is not required to perform Hajj next year.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The pilgrim in the state of Ihram
key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: A camel (specifically a young female camel)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for a Muhrim who has intercourse with his wife during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's chain clarifies the distinction between *tamm* (full penetration) and *duna al-farj* (partial intercourse) in the context of Ihram, establishing that while a camel (*badana*) is due in both scenarios, the obligation to repeat Hajj (*hujjat al-ilf*) applies only to full penetration. This ruling is central to Shia fiqh regarding the validity of the primary Hajj versus the compensatory sacrifice, reflecting the Imams' precise legal categorization of marital acts during the sacred state. The narration underscores the principle that minor infractions incur financial penalty without invalidating the ritual, whereas major ones require both sacrifice and ritual repetition.
